clues: This city in Albania sits on the bank of a river on a wide plain. Low hills rise to the southeast, with one river to the north and one to the south.
The near sea to the west shapes each season. This gives it a Mediterranean climate all year long.
A rich clan built this town in past times. In 1864 a man named Omer made it a real town.
Close by lie the stone ruins of the old town of Apollonia. Greek settlers built it long ago in 588 BCE.
This is the seventh largest city in the whole country. It is also the seat of its county and its town hall.
